post.caption: Baseball's first ring held one diamond. Before 1922, World Series winners got pins and medals instead. That year, the New York Giants beat the Yankees. The Giants received the first World Series rings. The ring was 14 karat gold with one diamond in the center. The sides read Giants World Champions 1922. Rings with one diamond stayed the norm for about 50 years. In 1972, the Oakland Athletics ring held a full carat diamond. In 1977, the Yankees ring spelled NY in many diamonds. As a player, Yogi Berra won 10 World Series rings, a record.
